notes: Verified all three rejection items against source: internal/proxy/mcp_oauth.go:177-198 mcpOAuthState() takes no request; the resource is config (mcp.oauth.resource) or the Keycloak RedirectURI origin, and st.Reason closes the door when both are empty. The aud accepted list (mcp_oauth.go:345-349) is built only from that config-derived resource, mcp.oauth.audience, and the web client id; r.URL.Path can only be /mcp or /mcp/gateway (exact mux patterns).

Refusal log (mcp_oauth.go:316) carries request_id=traceIDFromRequest(r), which withTrace (server.go:2730) pinned as X-Request-ID; TestMCPOAuthRefusalLogsTheCause asserts message, raw cause (signature/issuer/expired/audience/unlinked), a non-empty request_id equal to the response header, and the caller-supplied X-Request-ID case.

Ran the two mcp_oauth tests against the pre-fix mcp_oauth.go (943feab^): both fail (Host-derived resource made status active=true; no request_id). Against the fixed tree, `go test -race ./internal/proxy -run 'MCPOAuth|Keycloak'` and the full `go test ./internal/...` pass. keycloak_cache_test.go does not compile against the old keycloak.go (new symbols), but by reading: the cache-hit test holds the IdP with an unknown-kid fetch in flight and requires the known-kid lookup to return within 1s — impossible with the old lock-during-fetch code.

keycloak.go: locks now guard lookup/store only; fetches run unlocked on the caller ctx; stale entries return immediately with one background refresh (context.Background()+8s); failed discovery / JWKS fetch and unknown kids are negatively cached for 30s, and a cancelled caller ctx is not recorded as an IdP failure. Race detector clean.

Known trade-off (journal's uncertain item): after any JWKS fetch, a kid it does not list is refused without refetch for 30s, so tokens signed with a freshly rotated Keycloak key can be refused for up to 30s after the gateway's last fetch. Standard min-refresh-interval behaviour; self-heals; not a defect.

Minor, non-blocking: concurrent unknown-kid requests before the first fetch completes each fetch the JWKS (no singleflight) — strictly better than the old code, which refetched on every unknown kid. Commit 92bc502 (web/scripts/run-tool.mjs, --silent handling for pnpm) is scope drift unrelated to MCP OAuth; it is small, tested (node --test passes, tsc -b passes), and only changes how tsc/vite are invoked.

Protected-file checks: mcp.oauth.enabled defaults false and additionally requires AUTH_ENABLED, Keycloak SSO on, and a config-derived resource; the only new public route is the RFC 9728 metadata document, which 404s while inactive; no account creation, no role from token, inactive accounts refused, empty scope intersection refused, subject-only identity mapping; no secrets in status/log/error output; no migrations; no redirects. Web SsoTab vitest (26 tests) passes.

Privacy: refusal logs and audit events record client IP and the IdP subject id for security diagnostics — same purpose and retention as the existing auth audit events; no new personal-data category is introduced.
